✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: It's an enjoyable and refreshing spin on the well-trodden Fibonacci problem.
The solution is simple, but requires some efficiency in your approach to avoid recursion-hell.
Great clash!

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: The fact that computing the number of recursive calls to Fibonacci is similar to Fibonacci itself is so great. Had a solution resembling:

a, b = 1, 1
for _ in range(n - 1):
  a, b = b, a + b + 1

Where b is the result. Fun stuff!

I tried solving this puzzle with two different solutions I could think of. The first being the most obvious witch is by actually implementing and counting recursive calls, and the second was to count using breadth first search since the calls form a binary tree. Both solutions timed out after "Slower". I spent some time trying to figure out the math but I couldn't get it so I had to give up or else my head was gonna explode :P . Anyway, that was my experience and I'll need to study your solution later because I still don't get it.

Goal
* 1st paragraph: Please add "(other than the initial two)" after "each number".

* Consider rewording the middle paragraph to avoid mixing one level of recursion with another:

Whenever n > 1, a call to fib(n) recursively calls fib(n-1) and fib(n-2). Those calls recursively call fib() in the same way until reaching fib(0) or fib(1), which return immediately.

Cases
* Trivial 2 (Validator 7): Please change n to 0.

* Please move the Trivial 1 and Trivial 2 case pairs so that they appear consecutively.

* Impossible (Validator 11) is the only case whose output isn't a 32-bit integer. Please modify the test so that it features the same scenario.

Thanks.
Interesting, I had engineered the test cases such that implementing the pseudocode directly would only fail at "Improbable" (validator) / "Impossible" (test). Which language did you use?

To make it extra clear (but optional), you could probably add the following to the output spec:

> The number of fib() calls [...], including the initial call / the top-most call itself.
Only thing I'd suggest is writing a less-golfed solution so that cheaters can't just copy it from the contribution.

I don't think we can really stop someone from using AI for this clash to write golfed code (it worked for me in Python), but I've changed my solution anyway,

Probably won't be rewriting solutions again like this anytime soon.
Thanks for the feedback @Cakeisalie5! I've incorporated your suggestion :)
Lua and JS. But you're right. These tests and validators after "Slower" takes too long for unoptimized solutions. In my experience, fib recursion passed on "Improbable" but the BFS didn't
@jonas_melo I've updated my solution, let me know if it's any clearer 😉

yep, determine_number_of_fib_calls_to_compute_fib_n makes perfect sense to me.
